outcome: Perinatal outcomes (specifically comparison between appropriate-for-GA and small-for-GA neonates)
cohort: The study enrolled 87 consecutive singleton pregnancies, including 50 normotensive and 37 preeclamptic cases, stratified by gestational age for comparison.
finding: Both early- and late-onset preeclampsia pregnancies exhibited significantly lower placental VIMV compared to normotensive pregnancies, while no significant differences in VIMV were observed between early- and late-onset PE or between AGA and SGA neonates within PE pregnancies.
birth_weight: Babies were categorized as appropriate-for-GA (AGA) and small-for-GA (SGA) neonates.
gest_age: Gestational age was a key stratification factor, with groups defined as <34 weeks and >=34 weeks.
